study_identification_part.si_4_title: A normative modelling approach reveals age-atypical cortical thickness in a subgroup of males with autism spectrum disorder

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Local polynomial regression (LOESS) with smoothing kernel optimized over the age range.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: We used a local polynomial regression fitting procedure (LOESS) 34,35 , where the local width or smoothing kernel of the regression was determined by the model that provided the overall smallest sum of squared errors using hyperparameter optimization across 5 -100% of the full age range

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Primary response variable was cortical thickness (CT); the same method was also applied to gyrification, cortical volume, and surface area.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text:
Here we focus specifically on a neural feature of cortical morphology known as CT.
To show applicability of this approach we also applied the same method to other measures of neuroanatomy; gyrification, volume and surface area.

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Age was the explanatory variable for normative modeling of CT.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: Normative modelling of age-related CT effects was done utilizing male-only data from the typically developing group (TD)
